decisions.what: VERIFIED the current Claude Code plugin packaging format from the live docs before scaffolding, per operating_rules_for_implementing_agent. Fetched https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/plugins-reference and https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/plugins; BOTH now 301-redirect to code.claude.com, so the authoritative pages actually read were https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins. Verified, verbatim from those pages: (1) the plugin manifest is `plugin.json` inside a `.claude-plugin/` directory at the plugin root; it is OPTIONAL, and if present only `name` is required (kebab-case, used as the skill namespace); common optional fields are displayName, version, description, author{name,email,url}, homepage, repository, license, keywords, plus component-path overrides skills/commands/agents/hooks/mcpServers/lspServers/outputStyles. (2) Skills are auto-discovered from a `skills/` directory at the PLUGIN ROOT as `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, each with YAML frontmatter whose keys include name, description, model, disable-model-invocation; the docs explicitly warn that skills/, commands/, agents/ and hooks/ must NOT be placed inside `.claude-plugin/` — only plugin.json goes there. (3) MCP servers are declared in `.mcp.json` at the plugin root (or inline under an `mcpServers` key in plugin.json) with the shape {"mcpServers":{"<id>":{"command":..., "args":[...], "env":{...}}}}, and the substitutions ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}, ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} are available inside it. (4) `claude --plugin-dir ./x-agent` loads a plugin for local testing and `claude plugin validate ./x-agent` checks it. The scaffold matches this exactly: x-agent/.claude-plugin/plugin.json + x-agent/.mcp.json + x-agent/skills/wp-blocks/ (skill authored by the M7 track).
decisions.why: The spec forbids trusting memory for packaging. Recording the redirect chain matters: the docs.claude.com URLs named in the spec are no longer canonical.

decisions.what: The 16-tool table is declared in mcp/src/registry.ts and the six session/oracle/factory tools are loaded through a dynamic, failure-tolerant loader (loadExternalHandlers). The loader probes src/tools/<base>.{ts,js,mjs,mts} on disk with fs.existsSync and imports via pathToFileURL, so tsc never resolves a file that does not exist yet, and ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND / a syntax error / a module exporting no ToolDef all degrade to 'keep the not_implemented placeholder'.
decisions.why: Two agents implement tools in one package without editing each other's files, and `tools/list` must be complete (all 16, with schemas) before the second track's modules exist.

decisions.what: Every companion request carries the expected fingerprint in an `X-Expected-Fingerprint` request header, in addition to TreeIR.epoch on POST /validate.
decisions.why: CONTRACT.md §8 says 'every companion call carries the expected fingerprint' but only pins a mechanism for /validate (the tree's own epoch field). A request header is additive, ignored by any companion build that does not read it, and gives the mock a way to exercise the HTTP-409 epoch-conflict branch.

decisions.what: wp_validate and wp_spec_validate declare deliberately permissive MCP input schemas (z.looseObject with z.unknown().optional() fields carrying rich descriptions) and re-parse strictly inside the handler.
decisions.why: Both tools exist to REPORT schema violations as Diagnostics. A strict MCP input guard would turn every E_TREE_SCHEMA / E_SPEC_SCHEMA case into {code:'invalid_input'} and the tool would never be able to do its job. Handlers receive the original, unstripped arguments for the same reason.

decisions.what: W_UNQUANTIZED checks palette colours, spacing step sizes, typography sizes and layout.contentSize/wideSize against quantization_log[].snapped_to, compared as strings. Font FAMILIES are deliberately excluded.
decisions.why: The agent spec says 'tokens_candidates values all appear in quantization_log'. A font family is a chosen identifier, not a measured value snapped onto a scale, so requiring a quantization entry for it would be noise. Exported as quantizableValues() and asserted in tests.

decisions.what: E_BOX_OVERLAP slack is 2% of the PARENT box's width (for x/left-right) and height (for y/top-bottom), applied outward on all four edges. One diagnostic per offending child, listing every breached edge.
decisions.why: The spec says '2% slack' without naming the reference dimension; the parent is the only stable one (a zero-height child would otherwise get zero slack). Boundary behaviour is pinned by tests at slack+1 and slack-1.

decisions.what: wp_connect returns `suites` as plain slug strings (manifest.suites[].slug), dropping the version.
decisions.why: The spec pins the output type as `suites: string[]`. The versions remain available in full via wp_manifest.

decisions.what: wp_tokens_apply additionally returns `theme_json_preview` (the local emitter output) and `diff_against_instance`, and accepts `dry_run: true`.
decisions.why: The spec places templates/theme-json/emitter.ts on this side specifically 'for local preview/diff'. Surfacing it on the tool makes the extend-tier write rehearsable at zero cost and zero risk, which matters because the write is posture-gated and irreversible.

decisions.what: The build emits to mcp/dist/ with rootDir = the plugin root, so the server entry point is mcp/dist/mcp/src/server.js (referenced from .mcp.json). A `prepare` script runs the build on npm install, and no dist/ is left checked in.
decisions.why: templates/theme-json/emitter.ts lives outside mcp/ by spec, so rootDir must cover both; nesting is the honest consequence. A committed dist would silently go stale as the second track adds tool modules.

decisions.what: The vitest root is x-agent/ while the package is x-agent/mcp/; tsconfig maps the bare `vitest` specifier via compilerOptions.paths.
decisions.why: file_layout pins tests at x-agent/tests/ and the package at x-agent/mcp/. Node resolution cannot walk from x-agent/tests/ into x-agent/mcp/node_modules; Vitest self-aliases at runtime but tsc needs the explicit path mapping to type-check the suite.

decisions.what: tests/schemas.test.ts ships an inline JSON-Schema validator (no ajv) covering type/type-arrays, required, properties, additionalProperties, items, enum, const, pattern, minimum, exclusiveMinimum, oneOf and $ref (both #/definitions/... and the cross-file x-contract/<file>#/... form). It also asserts the vendored schemas use NO keyword outside that set.
decisions.why: The task pinned a smaller subset, but the vendored schemas actually use minimum/exclusiveMinimum/oneOf and a cross-file $ref (design-spec -> design-tokens). The keyword-coverage assertion means a future schema edit that introduces an unenforced keyword fails the suite instead of silently weakening the drift check.

deviations.spec_ref: agent-plugin.spec.json milestones.M1_scaffold ('all 16 tools') vs mcp_tools[] (15 entries)
deviations.what: mcp_tools[] enumerates 15 tools: wp_connect, wp_manifest, wp_patterns, wp_validate, wp_compile, wp_render, wp_verify, wp_screenshot, wp_spec_validate, wp_tokens_apply, wp_block_scaffold, wp_block_build_test, wp_block_install, wp_parse, wp_snapshot. Registered a 16th, `wp_disconnect`, to reconcile the count: it closes the warm Playwright session, drops the block factory, clears the manifest/pattern/fingerprint caches and forgets the pinned connection overrides.
deviations.why: M1's acceptance says 'shows all 16 tools with input schemas'. wp_disconnect is the natural missing counterpart to wp_connect — without it there is no way to switch instances or recover from an instance rebuilt underneath a warm session. It is also the disposal hook the session track needs (registerSessionProvider().dispose).

deviations.what: Added two agent-local error codes beyond the nine pinned ones: `not_implemented` (a tool is declared in the registry but its handler module is absent from this build) and `internal` (an unexpected agent-side throw, wrapped rather than leaked).
deviations.why: §7's list covers failures of the agent<->companion interaction; neither of these is one. They never travel to the companion and never appear in a companion request. `not_implemented` is required by the parallel-track seam: a missing handler must be a structured call-time error, not a missing tool at list time. `internal` is required by the 'never a bare throw to the client' rule — something has to catch a TypeError.

deviations.spec_ref: agent-plugin.spec.json fixtures.authoring_rule ('ground-truth markup fixtures are CAPTURED, not hand-written')
deviations.what: fixtures/trees/*.json are hand-authored; NO golden markup was authored. fixtures/golden/*.html and fixtures/images/hero-sample.png do not exist yet.
deviations.why: The authoring rule forbids hand-written expected MARKUP, which is exactly what was avoided — there is no expected-markup fixture anywhere in this track. Input trees and Design Spec IRs are agent inputs, not compiler ground truth, so they are legitimately authored. Capturing the golden markup requires a real Playground editor (tests/capture-golden.ts, M3) and belongs to the session track.

deviations.what: wp_manifest's output schema is the Manifest shape with `blocks` widened to a record of unknown, plus the added fields summary, filtered, blocks_returned, blocks_total, served_from_cache.
deviations.why: The same spec entry mandates a summary mode returning 'names+parents only', which by construction cannot satisfy manifest.schema.json's per-block required[] (title, category, api_version, attributes, is_dynamic). The widening is confined to the blocks map; every other Manifest field is still validated strictly. The added booleans make the cache and filter behaviour observable to the calling agent.

seams_exposed_for_the_session_track.context: mcp/src/context.ts — exports `interface Ctx {config, companion, manifestCache, logger, runtime, session?: unknown, factory?: unknown}`, `class Runtime`, `registerSessionProvider(p)`, `registerFactoryProvider(p)`, `getSession(ctx)`, `getFactory(ctx)`, `interface Provider {create, dispose?, onEpochChange?}`. Full contract in a comment block at the top of the file. Both declaration merging (`declare module './context.js' { interface Ctx { session?: HarnessSession } }`) and the provider hooks are supported.
seams_exposed_for_the_session_track.registry: mcp/src/registry.ts — exports `type ToolDef`, `const TOOLS: ToolDef[]` (stable array identity; mutated in place by the loader), `loadExternalHandlers()`, `findTool()`, `unimplementedToolNames()`, `isUnimplemented()`. Session-track modules export `tools: ToolDef[]` (or any named ToolDef export, or a default export) from src/tools/{compile,verify,screenshot,blockScaffold,blockBuildTest,blockInstall}.ts; a matching `name` replaces the declared entry wholesale, an unknown `name` is appended.
seams_exposed_for_the_session_track.companion: mcp/src/companion.ts — the ONLY HTTP surface. fetchFingerprint, fetchManifest, validate, parse, render, patterns, harnessHtml, harnessUrl, harnessUrlAlternate, basicCredentials, authHeader, installBlockFromFile, installBlockBytes, blocksLibrary, rollbackBlock, deleteBlock, themeTokens, snapshotExport, reset; plus `stats` and `onEpochEvent` for observability and `class ManifestCache`.
seams_exposed_for_the_session_track.local_flag: A ToolDef that needs no connection must set `local: true` (wp_block_scaffold and wp_block_build_test should). Without it a call with no resolvable config fails with invalid_input before the handler runs.
